evidence.r1: Glass is confined to navigation, dates, venue selection, ticket action and the venue menu; film content is on flat surfaces.
evidence.r2: The venue menu sits below its trigger without overlapping another glass surface, and selected rows use fills.
evidence.r3: The navigation and programme controls are a limited set with distinct wayfinding or booking roles.
evidence.r4: The navigation, date group and venue menu use the same cloudy light regular-glass appearance.
evidence.r5: No clear-glass surface is visible; the controls are pale and diffusely frosted over the still.
evidence.r6: Only Book tickets has a tinted background; the selected date uses a neutral dark fill.
evidence.r7: The normal navigation and venue menu show diffuse image-dependent shading rather than opaque flat replacement surfaces.
evidence.r8: The large navigation has fixed rounded corners, dates use rounded rectangles and Book tickets is a capsule.
evidence.r9: The selected date has tighter inset corners, and the selected venue outline follows the outer menu corner.
evidence.r10: The standalone Book tickets action is a capsule and the dense date controls are rounded rectangles.
evidence.r11: Navigation, dates, venues and booking form four separate glass groups across the top bar.
evidence.r12: The navigation and date groups contain text buttons, with no independent icon button sharing their backgrounds.
evidence.r13: The material spans the navigation and date controls themselves rather than their text labels.
evidence.r14: The dates form a single continuous strip and the venue control is deliberately separated from it.
evidence.r15: The two scrolled captures show one soft fade at the upper content edge under the controls.
evidence.r16: The opening-film image remains visible behind the top controls in both lower-page captures.
evidence.r17: Programme headings and venue labels sit beneath the resting top controls in the scrolled captures.
evidence.r18: The light navigation is readable, but the captures do not establish numerical contrast in a dark mode.
evidence.r19: The reduced-transparency top controls remain readable, but increased contrast and reduced motion are not shown.
evidence.r20: The film still fills the first window and the programme background extends edge to edge below it.
evidence.r21: The hero copy clears the top controls and the scrolled upper edge extends the film image behind them.
evidence.r22: The navigation and venue menu show their material rims without a distinct custom backing panel.
evidence.r23: The venue-menu still does not reveal whether opening morphs or whether presses glow and flex.
evidence.r24: Navigation and menu text are monochrome; the ticket tint is a background rather than a coloured label.
evidence.r25: Dark navigation and venue labels contrast with the pale image-derived glass backgrounds.
